items.title: A representable morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces is representable by schemes and affine

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces is in fact representable by schemes and affine (statement lines 4208-4213). The proof shows affineness by testing against morphisms from affine schemes: both the source and the target are written as filtered colimits of affine schemes, a morphism from an affine scheme into the target factors through one of its stages, quasi-compactness of the morphism makes the fibre product quasi-compact so that the projection to the source factors through one of its stages, and after increasing the chosen stage of the target the fibre product is identified with a fibre product of affine schemes, hence is affine (proof lines 4215-4236). Representability by schemes then follows from the locality criterion for affineness (proof lines 4215-4217). The claim is H2: the argument is a sequence of factorisations through stages, each justified by a named statement, ending in the identification of the fibre product with the fibre product of two affine schemes.
